text_blocks.snippet: In CPR, a 15:2 ratio refers to the compression-to-ventilation ratio used by two rescuers performing CPR on a child (1 year to puberty). This means they perform 15 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. For a single rescuer performing CPR on a child, the ratio is 30:2.

list.snippet: Child CPR: Refers to CPR performed on children from 1 year old up to the onset of puberty.
15:2 Ratio: This ratio is used when two rescuers are present and performing CPR on a child.
30:2 Ratio: This ratio is used when a single rescuer is performing CPR on a child.
Compression Depth: For children, compressions should be about 1/3 the depth of the chest, or approximately 2 inches (5cm).
Compression Rate: The rate should be maintained between 100-120 compressions per minute.
Rescue Breaths: Rescue breaths should be given for about 1 second, ensuring the chest rises visibly.
Complete Chest Recoil: After each compression, the chest should be allowed to recoil fully.
Rescuer Roles: When two rescuers are present, one can focus on compressions while the other manages ventilations and AED (if available).
Importance of Coordination: Two rescuers should coordinate their efforts to ensure high-quality CPR and effective ventilations.
